clues: This city sits on the south coast of its land, where the shore meets a wide gulf of the Atlantic Ocean. Sandy beaches line its edge.
The air here stays warm all year, and the rains come and go with the seasons. Its climate is drier than the wet coast towns near it.
In 1877, this city took the capital job from an older coast town. It has held the job of capital ever since that year.
This city's name grew from an old word for ants. Tall red anthills dotted the land round about, full of busy soldier ants on the move.
The parliament of Ghana meets in this city. Its top court sits here too, and the land is run from here.
